page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Protostomia
steps.why: The two groups differ in one event of development — what the blastopore becomes — so the answer is that one fact stated twice, once for each group.
common_mistakes: Writing that the blastopore becomes the anus in Protostomia. Proto means first, and the mouth forms first.
Giving Echinodermata as an example. It is a deuterostome.
steps.memory_tip: Proto means first and stoma means mouth: in Protostomia the mouth comes first.
steps.margin_note: The blastopore fact and the three phyla. Three lines.
lines: These are eumetazoans in which the blastopore
of the embryo develops into the mouth.
The anus is formed later, as a new opening.

steps.label: Deuterostomia
steps.why: Deutero means second, so in this group the mouth is the second opening to form and the blastopore end is left as the anus.
common_mistakes: Swapping the example groups. Chordata, which includes humans, is deuterostome.
steps.memory_tip: Deutero means second: the mouth is the second opening, so the blastopore end becomes the anus.
steps.margin_note: The same fact reversed, plus the three phyla. Keep both halves the same length.
lines: These are eumetazoans in which the anus is
formed from or near the blastopore.
The mouth is formed later, as a new opening.

insider_note: Write it as a two-row table — what the blastopore becomes, then the example phyla — because a table shows the difference faster than a paragraph.
